title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 37 (Action by affected persons)

content.overview: Section 37 provides that a suit may be filed or any other action may be taken under section 34 or section 35 or section 36 by any person, group of persons or any association of persons affected by any misleading statement or the inclusion or omission of any matter in the prospectus.
content.glance: Affected persons (individual, group or association) may file a suit or take any other action under ss. 34, 35 or 36 for prospectus defects; s. 37 is a standing provision, not a separate liability head.
content.study: Section 37 does not create a new species of liability. It enables any person, group of persons or any association of persons affected by any misleading statement or the inclusion or omission of any matter in the prospectus to file a suit or take any other action under section 34 (criminal liability for mis-statements), section 35 (civil liability for mis-statements) or section 36 (punishment for fraudulently inducing persons to invest money), as the case may be. Current-law framing: identify the affected claimant class; identify the prospectus defect (misleading statement, inclusion or omission); choose the correct substantive section (34/35/36); then apply that section’s ingredients and remedies.

sections.heading: Standing
sections.body: Any person, group of persons or any association of persons affected by any misleading statement or the inclusion or omission of any matter in the prospectus may sue or take action.

sections.heading: Substantive routes
sections.body: The suit or other action is under section 34, section 35 or section 36 — not under section 37 as an independent cause of action.

sections.heading: Application
sections.body: Prove affected status; map the prospectus defect to the chosen substantive section; seek that section’s remedy.

examples.title: Investor group civil claim
examples.body: A group of subscribers affected by a misleading statement in the prospectus brings a compensation claim under section 35. Section 37 confirms their standing as affected persons.

examples.title: Association action
examples.body: An association of affected investors relies on section 37 to pursue remedies under sections 34–36 on the basis of prospectus defects.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 37 itself create liability for misleading statements?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It is a standing/action provision. Liability and remedies come from sections 34, 35 or 36.

misconceptions.trap: Section 37 is a freestanding liability provision.
misconceptions.correction: It only enables affected persons to take action under sections 34, 35 or 36.

misconceptions.trap: Only individual investors can sue under s. 37.
misconceptions.correction: The section expressly covers any person, group of persons or any association of persons.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 37 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the affected person / group / association. II. Identify the prospectus defect (misleading statement, inclusion or omission). III. Choose s. 34, 35 or 36. IV. Apply that section’s ingredients and remedies. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Affected status; prospectus defect; chosen substantive section (34/35/36); remedy sought.

examTips: Treat s. 37 as standing, not liability.
Always pair it with s. 34, 35 or 36.
Note that groups and associations of affected persons are expressly covered.
revisionPoints: Standing of affected persons (individual, group, association)
